bib.title: Make-An-Audio: Text-To-Audio Generation with Prompt-Enhanced Diffusion Models

question: How can text-to-audio generation be made high-fidelity despite scarce text-audio pairs and the length of raw waveforms, and can the same model take audio, image and video as input?
hypothesis: Generating captions for language-free audio (distill-then-reprogram) plus a spectrogram latent diffusion model with CLAP conditioning will outperform prior text-to-audio systems.
contributions: Latent diffusion with a spectrogram autoencoder to model long continuous audio
Pseudo prompt enhancement (distill-then-reprogram) to use language-free audio
Study of text representations, favouring CLAP for efficiency
Generalisation to X-to-Audio (text, audio inpainting, image, video)

method.summary: A mel-spectrogram autoencoder compresses audio to a 4-channel latent; a U-Net latent diffusion model conditioned on a frozen CLAP text encoder (cross-attention, classifier-free guidance) generates latents; a HiFi-GAN vocoder converts mel to waveform. Captions for unlabeled audio come from captioning and retrieval experts filtered by CLAP score, and training examples are concatenated online with sampled sound events.

datasets.name: Combined training set (15 sources, Table 4)
datasets.split: AudioCaps-train used; AudioSet filtered to reduce speech and music
datasets.source: AudioSet, BBC sound effects, Audiostock, AudioCaps, ESC-50, FSD50K, Free To Use Sounds, Sonniss, WeSoundEffects, MACS, Epidemic Sound, UrbanSound8K, WavText5Ks, LibriSpeech/LibriTTS, Medley-solos-DB
datasets.preprocessing: 16 kHz, pad to 10 s, FFT 1024, hop 256, mel 80x624; text normalisation; class labels discarded then replaced by pseudo prompts

models.name: Make-An-Audio (CLAP)
models.architecture: spectrogram autoencoder + latent diffusion U-Net + frozen CLAP text encoder + HiFi-GAN vocoder

models.name: Make-An-Audio BERT / T5-Large / CLIP variants
models.architecture: same with other frozen text encoders

models.name: Diffsound
models.architecture: discrete diffusion on VQ-VAE codes, CLIP text

training.objective: Diffusion noise-prediction MSE; autoencoder: reconstruction + GAN + KL losses; text dropout 20% for classifier-free guidance
training.lr: 0.005 base, scaled by number of GPUs and batch size following LDM
training.regularisation: dynamic reprogramming (N in {0,1,2} concatenated events); text encoder frozen

other.unconditional_finetune: base model fine-tuned so 20% of text sequences are empty
other.inpainting: model explicitly fine-tuned for inpainting; masks: LaMa irregular thin/medium/thick and wav2vec2 frame masks p=30/50/70%

inference.decoding: latent diffusion with classifier-free guidance, scale s>=1

parameters.sdedit_t0: t0 in [0.2,0.5] works well for personalised generation
parameters.video: 4 uniformly picked frames, CLIP features pooled

metrics.name: CLAP score
metrics.definition: reference-free audio-text alignment, adapted from CLIP score

metrics.name: MOS-Q / MOS-F
metrics.definition: Amazon Mechanical Turk raters, 20-100 Likert scale, 95% CI; quality and faithfulness

eval.protocol: Number of raters and samples per MOS test not stated; $8/hour, about $750 total; no seeds.

availability.data: demo page https://Text-to-Audio.github.io; training data from public sources

limits: Authors concede iterative sampling is slow and latent diffusion needs substantial compute, with degradation at smaller training data.
Only Diffsound is a baseline (stated as the only publicly available T2A model); AudioGen is not compared.
Number of MOS raters, sampling steps, guidance scale, batch size, optimizer and seeds are not stated.
Visual-to-audio uses a 110h FSD50K-trained variant, and quality (video MOS-Q 60.0) is below reference.
Text claims Make-An-Audio has the highest CLAP, but Table 1 shows T5-Large at 0.486 above 0.482.
Table 5 is cited in text as the dataset table, but dataset statistics are Table 4 (appendix numbering slip).

terms.definition: distill-then-reprogram: captions from expert models selected by CLAP score, then online concatenation with sampled events
each time N concepts are sampled from database D, N in {0,1,2}, and concatenated to the original pair by template
